result.title: Semantic Saliency from Multi-Modal Large Language Model Scene Understanding Maps
result.summary: Image-computable low-level image saliency has shaped perceptual psychology and computer science, but is limited by its inability to capture human high-level cognitive factors that influence attention and eye movements. Here, we propose a new fully automated method to compute semantic saliency by quantifying each object's contribution to scene comprehension without fitting any parameters to human data: the Automated Scene Understanding Map (AUTO-SUM). AUTO-SUM automatically segments and removes individual objects from a scene, uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to describe the original and modified scenes, and measures the semantic similarity between these descriptions using text embeddings. We show that AUTO-SUM can predict which object is most important in a human-measured scene understanding map (H-SUM) estimated using human scene descriptions. We also show that AUTO-SUM can predict the object most fixated by human observers during free viewing and scene description tasks better than a low-level saliency model (GBVS, Itti-Koch), a saliency model trained based on human meaning ratings (Meaning Map), and comparable to DeepGaze, which is trained on human fixation data. We contend that AUTO-SUM can be used as a semantic saliency model that complements lower-level saliency models. Code are available at https://github.com/starsky77/AUTO-SUM-Source-Code .

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AUTO-SUM：自动分割并移除场景中的单个物体，用 MLLM 分别描述原图与修改后图像，再以文本嵌入度量两段描述的语义相似度，从而量化各物体对场景理解的贡献，并在人类场景理解图与自由观看/描述任务的注视数据上验证其预测能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「移除物体—描述差异」的反事实归因流程，可能为 LVR 中判断哪些视觉细节被保留、如何筛选关键视觉证据或做贡献分配提供可核查的测量线索；但论文目标是预测人类显著性与注视，与推理状态生成无直接关联。
